s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute bilateral visual disturbance with transient visual obscuration and tinnitus, associated with optic disc edema and posterior fossa abnormalities
salient_findings: Bilateral blurry vision with transient visual obscurations
key_facts: 3-month history of bilateral blurry vision
Transient visual obscurations
1-month history of tinnitus
Bilateral optic disc edema
Optic disc edema worse in the right eye
Fundus photography shows florid optic nerve edema with disc hemorrhages and exudates in the right eye
Fundus photography shows less severe optic nerve edema in the left eye
MRI brain shows multiple cysts in the posterior fossa
Large cyst at the level of the fourth ventricle measuring 1.2 cm × 1.6 cm
Obstructive hydrocephalus
CSF analysis shows no protein, white blood cells, or organisms

salient_findings: Bilateral blurry vision with transient visual obscurations
key_facts: 3-month history of bilateral blurry vision

shortlist.label: Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral optic disc edema and transient visual obscurations are classic symptoms

shortlist.label: Arachnoid Cyst
shortlist.why_kept: MRI findings of multiple cysts in the posterior fossa, including a large cyst at the level of the fourth ventricle, are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Dandy-Walker Malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Posterior fossa abnormalities, including cysts and obstructive hydrocephalus, are characteristic of this condition

shortlist.label: Pseudotumor Cerebri
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to idiopathic intracranial hypertension, with symptoms including bilateral optic disc edema and transient visual obscurations

shortlist.label: Craniopharyngioma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, this tumor can cause obstructive hydrocephalus and visual disturbances due to its location near the optic nerves

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of bilateral blurry vision, transient visual obscurations, and optic disc edema are consistent with increased intracranial pressure, and the absence of protein, white blood cells, or organisms in the CSF analysis supports this diagnosis. The presence of obstructive hydrocephalus due to the cysts could contribute to the increased intracranial pressure.

rejected.label: Arachnoid Cyst
rejected.why: While the patient has a large cyst at the level of the fourth ventricle, the primary symptoms and findings are more suggestive of increased intracranial pressure rather than a direct effect of the cyst itself.

rejected.label: Dandy-Walker Malformation
rejected.why: This condition typically presents in infancy or early childhood with symptoms of hydrocephalus and cerebellar malformation, which does not match the patient's age and presentation.

rejected.label: Pseudotumor Cerebri
rejected.why: This is another term for Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension, so it is not a distinct alternative.

rejected.label: Craniopharyngioma
rejected.why: This is a type of brain tumor that could cause increased intracranial pressure, but the description of multiple cysts in the posterior fossa and the lack of a specific mention of a tumor mass makes this less likely than Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension.
